'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Insurgency in the Maghreb (2002–present)|Insurgency in the Maghreb]]
**A [[President of France|French presidency]] official and a senior [[government of Chad|Chadian official]] announce that [[Chad]] will reinforce their troops by 1,000 in order to fight [[jihadist]]s in the border regions of [[Mali]], [[Niger]], and [[Burkina Faso]]. It will be formally announced in a summit on February 15–16. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-sahel-security/chad-reinforces-troops-against-militants-in-sahel-as-france-mulls-changes-idUSKBN2AC12V?il=0 (Reuters)]
*[[Mali War]]
**A [[Togo|Togolese]] [[United Nations peacekeeping|peacekeeper]] has died after being wounded yesterday in an attack on a [[United Nations Multidimensional Integrated Stabilization Mission in Mali|MINUSMA]] base near [[Douentza]] in [[Mopti Region|Mopti]], central [[Mali]], which wounded 28 peacekeepers, according to [[United Nations]] spokesperson [[Stéphane Dujarric]]. [https://www.urdupoint.com/en/world/un-peacekeeper-dies-after-wednesdays-attack-1166968.html (UrduPoint)]

'''Arts and culture'''
*[[Aftermath of the January 6 United States Capitol attack|Aftermath of the 2021 storming of the United States Capitol]]
**The [[United States Senate]] votes by [[unanimous consent]] to award [[United States Capitol Police]] officer [[Eugene Goodman (police officer)|Eugene Goodman]] the [[Congressional Gold Medal]] for keeping [[riot]]ers away from the [[United States Senate chamber|Senate chamber]] during the [[January 6 United States Capitol attack|storming]] of the [[United States Capitol]]. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/politics/capitol-riot-goodman-impeachment/2021/02/12/ae9f074e-6d89-11eb-9f80-3d7646ce1bc0_story.html (''The Washington Post'')]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic]], [[COVID-19 recession]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Norway]]
***The [[Norway|Norwegian]] [[Economy of Norway|economy]] contracts by 2.5% in 2020 due to the impact of the [[COVID-19 pandemic]], even as their Q4 [[gross domestic product|GDP]] grew faster than expected by 1.9%. [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2021-02-12/norway-gdp-even-stronger-than-expected-fanning-rate-hike-bets (Bloomberg)]
**[[Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom]]
***The [[Office for National Statistics]] says that the [[economy of the United Kingdom|economy]] of the [[United Kingdom]] has contracted by a record 9.9% since the [[pandemic]] began, but has narrowly avoided a [[Recession shapes#W-shaped|double-dip recession]]. This is nonetheless estimated to be the largest annual contraction since 1709. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/business-56037123 (BBC News)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*An [[earthquake]] of magnitude 5.9 strikes 35 kilometres west of [[Murghob]], [[Tajikistan]]. The tremors are felt as far away as northern [[India]] and [[Pakistan]]. [https://www.straitstimes.com/asia/south-asia/tajikistan-quake-shakes-north-india-pakistan-no-major-damage (''The Straits Times'')]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in North America]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in New York (state)|COVID-19 pandemic in New York]]
*****[[Governor of New York|New York governor]] [[Andrew Cuomo]] announces to extend the operating hours of indoor dining in [[restaurant]]s in [[New York City]] to 11:00 p.m. [[Eastern Time|EST]] beginning from [[Valentine's Day]] as it expands their curfew on restaurants and bars statewide. [https://newyork.cbslocal.com/2021/02/12/nyc-indoor-dining-returns/ (WCBS-TV)]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in New Hampshire]], [[Lineage B.1.1.7]]
*****[[New Hampshire]] reports their first case of the B.1.1.7 variant in a person from [[Hillsborough County, New Hampshire|Hillsborough County]] who had close contact with someone who travelled internationally. [https://patch.com/new-hampshire/concord-nh/first-case-uk-variant-coronavirus-found-new-hampshire (Patch.com)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Canada]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in British Columbia]]
*****[[British Columbia]] reports [[Canada]]'s first case of the Nigerian [[Variants of SARS-CoV-2|variant]] of [[Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2|SARS-CoV-2]] in a young person from the Interior Health region who is currently self-isolating. [https://vancouversun.com/news/local-news/covid-19-provincial-health-officer-says-nigerian-variant-identified-in-b-c (''Vancouver Sun'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Mexico]]
****[[Government of Mexico|Mexican authorities]] lower the pandemic alert level in [[Mexico City]] and the [[State of Mexico]] to orange status due to a decrease in the number of COVID-19 hospitalizations. [https://medicalxpress.com/news/2021-02-mexico-city-lowers-pandemic-status.html (MedicalXpress)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Cambodia]]
****[[Cambodia]] approves the emergency use of the [[Oxford-AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine|Oxford-AstraZeneca]] and [[Sinovac Biotech]] [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccines]]. [https://cambodianess.com/article/cambodia-approves-astrazeneca-and-sinovac-vaccines-for-covid-19-emergency-use (Cambodianess)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia]]
****The number of recovered [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]] patients in [[Indonesia]] surpasses one million. [https://health.detik.com/berita-detikhealth/d-5371801/kasus-sembuh-covid-19-ri-tembus-satu-juta-kasus-aktif-ada-165086 (detikHealth)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Japan]]
****Japan receives their first shipment of 400,000 doses of the [[Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine|Pfizer-BioNTech vaccine]] from [[Belgium]]. [https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2021/02/12/national/science-health/japan-approval-pfizer-vaccine/ (''The Japan Times'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Pakistan]]
****[[Pakistan]] approves the emergency use of [[China]]'s [[CanSino Biologics|CanSinoBio]] [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]], becoming the fourth [[vaccine]] to be approved in the country. [https://www.dawn.com/news/1606978/chinese-cansinobio-becomes-fourth-covid-19-vaccine-to-be-approved-for-emergency-use-in-pakistan (DAWN)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Greece]]
****[[Greece]] extends their full [[COVID-19 lockdowns|lockdown]] to [[Achaia]] and the island of [[Euboea]] beginning February 13 in an attempt to reduce the spread of [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]]. [https://www.ekathimerini.com/262329/article/ekathimerini/news/achaia-evia-join-attica-in-hard-lockdown (Ekathimerini)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Russia]], [[COVID-19 pandemic in Serbia]]
****[[Russia]] gives a preliminary approval for its [[Sputnik V COVID-19 vaccine|Sputnik V]] [[vaccine]] to be manufactured in [[Serbia]]. [https://www.themoscowtimes.com/2021/02/12/russia-gives-serbia-green-light-to-manufacture-sputnik-v-vaccine-a72927 (''The Moscow Times'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom]]
****The [[United Kingdom]] surpasses four million cases of [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]], becoming the fifth country to do so after the [[United States]], [[India]], [[Brazil]], and [[Russia]]. [https://www.independent.co.uk/news/uk/home-news/covid-cases-uk-coronavirus-update-b1801571.html (''The Independent'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Chile]]
***[[President of Chile|President]] [[Sebastián Piñera]] receives the first dose of the [[Sinovac]]'s [[CoronaVac]] vaccine. [http://www.uniindia.com/news/world/health-chile-prez-vaccination/2317582.html (United News of India)]

*[[Hong Kong–United Kingdom relations]], [[Censorship in Hong Kong]]
**[[Hong Kong]]'s public broadcaster [[Radio Television Hong Kong]] joins [[mainland China]] in blocking [[BBC World News]] and [[BBC World Service]]. [https://www.usnews.com/news/world/articles/2021-02-11/bbc-world-news-barred-from-airing-in-china-cgtn (U.S. News and World Report)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[2020–2021 United States racial unrest]], [[Black Lives Matter protests in New York City]]
**A [[Black Lives Matter]] protest turned violent in [[New York City]], resulting in nearly a dozen arrests and injuries among police officers. The [[New York Police Department]] said two officers were injured during the march in [[midtown Manhattan]]. [https://www.washingtonexaminer.com/news/blm-march-nyc-turns-violent-11-arrests-made (''The Washington Examiner'')]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2021 Italian government crisis]]
**[[Prime Minister of Italy|Prime Minister-designate]] [[Mario Draghi]] meets with [[President of Italy|President]] [[Sergio Mattarella]] and presents the list of proposed ministers for his [[cabinet of Italy|cabinet]]. Draghi's [[oath of office]] is scheduled for tomorrow at 12:00 p.m. local time. [https://www.ansa.it/sito/notizie/politica/2021/02/12/governo-draghi-mattarella-quirinale-ministri_8441e281-0ba6-48f1-b7bb-c7ac123fd7e0.html (ANSA)]
*[[2020–2021 Belarusian protests]], [[Elections in Belarus]]
**[[President of Belarus|President]] [[Alexander Lukashenko]] says that the [[Belarus|country]] will hold a [[referendum]] that would change their [[Constitution of Belarus|constitution]] before January 18, 2022. [https://apnews.com/article/alexander-lukashenko-belarus-constitutions-municipal-elections-elections-b3ddf44e529cc3a45320cc61d6dba3aa (AP)]
*[[North Korea]]n [[List of leaders of North Korea|Supreme Leader]] [[Kim Jong-un]] [[dismissal (employment)|fires]] Economic Affairs Minister [[Kim Tu-il]] less than a month after appointing him to his [[Cabinet of North Korea|cabinet]] for "lack of innovation". He is replaced by [[O Su-yong]], according to [[state media]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-northkorea-politics/north-koreas-kim-fires-new-economy-minister-blasts-cabinet-for-unambitious-plans-idUSKBN2AB2SV?il=0 (Reuters)]

'''Science and technology'''
*A study by [[University College London]] suggests that the [[bluestone]]s that form [[Stonehenge]] in [[Wiltshire]], England, likely [[Theories about Stonehenge|originated]] from another [[stone circle]] in [[Pembrokeshire]], Wales, called Waun Mawn. [https://www.dawn.com/news/1607093/stonehenge-likely-made-with-stones-from-older-monumen (AFP via ''Dawn'')]
*[[Facebook]] restricts the content posted by the [[Myanmar]]'s [[Tatmadaw]] in order to stop the spread of "misinformation" in a wake of [[2021 Myanmar coup d'état|military coup]]. [https://www.euronews.com/2021/02/12/facebook-limits-content-shared-by-myanmar-military-to-stop-the-spread-of-misinformation (Euronews)]
